title: OpenKNX test profile
description: A named, reviewable description of one test run: what is run, on which device, and what the run promises to cover. Read by Run-Tests.ps1 (-TestProfile <name>). The addresses come from Test-Bench-Config.json: device and traffic name a device there, rig.fromBench takes the bench values. A value given on the command line wins over the profile.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so an editor shows the field descriptions and checks the file.

name.description: The name the profile is started with: Run-Tests.ps1 -TestProfile <name>. A file without it is not a profile.

description.description: One sentence for the profile list (Run-Tests.ps1 -ListProfiles).

what.description: The stage the profile runs, as -What. All runs every stage, or the ones named in stages.

stages.description: Only with what = All: the stages to run, comma separated. Known stages: SelfTest, Dpt, HostStack, Conformance, Features, Rename, Busmonitor, Fidelity, DeviceState, Devices, Hardening, Legacy, Reference, EtsReadback, Speed. Without it every stage runs.

device.description: The device under test: the name of a device in Test-Bench-Config.json, or the values themselves.

traffic.description: The traffic interface of the run: the name of a device in Test-Bench-Config.json whose IP becomes -TrafficIp. It must sit on the TP line of the device under test. rig.trafficIp, when given, wins.

rig.description: The test rig around the device under test. Usually only fromBench plus the values that differ for this profile.

fromBench.description: Which values the profile takes from the rig block of Test-Bench-Config.json: "all", or a list of field names. A field written out in this profile wins over the bench value. Without fromBench nothing is taken.

trafficIp.description: Second interface that puts telegrams on the bus (-TrafficIp). It must sit on the TP line of the device under test.

guided.description: Allow cases that ask for a hand at the device or in ETS (-Guided).

includeDestructive.description: Allow cases that change device state; each one restores it (-IncludeDestructive).

iterations.description: Number of passes for what = Endurance (-Iterations). 0 leaves the default.

requires.description: What the profile promises to cover. Each entry names an argument that must have a value, from the profile or the command line; if one is missing the run is not started (exit 3), so a profile cannot report PASS over cases it never ran.

notes.description: Free text for the reader: what is special about this profile.
